summary: This section explains how accounting standards are set for companies in India. The Central Government has the power to officially set these rules. It does this based on recommendations from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and after checking with another official body.
points: The Central Government can prescribe accounting standards or any additions to them.
The standards must be recommended by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.
The Central Government must consult and examine recommendations from the National Financial Reporting Authority.
Until the National Financial Reporting Authority is set up, the government works with recommendations from the National Advisory Committee on Accounting Standards instead.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is preparing its yearly financial accounts. The directors want to know which rules to follow for reporting their money. According to the law, the company must follow the accounting standards prescribed by the Central Government. These standards are first recommended by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and examined by the National Financial Reporting Authority, or the older advisory committee if the new authority is not yet formed. Meera Textiles Private Limited ensures its accounts match these exact government rules.

terms.meaning: Official rules and guidelines for how companies must keep and report their financial accounts.
An addition or extra part put into a document.

watch: People often confuse which advisory body the government must consult before the new authority is fully created.
